title: Ray Bradbury BBC Radio
paragraphs: Curated 21-item BBC Ray Bradbury radio-drama collection spanning 1962-2014. It combines standalone BBC adaptations with the 12-episode 1995-97 Tales of the Bizarre run and later Radio 4 Dangerous Visions productions. Frozen rows have no broadcast dates; historical production dates are represented additively in archive profiles and claims.

GRH documents the program through Early BBC Bradbury adaptations (September 12, 1962 to May 3, 1968) on [[org|org.deepv2.f713a484394d0d32|BBC Radio]], 1982-1991 BBC adaptations (1982-03 to August 28, 1991) on [[org|org.deepv2.f713a484394d0d32|BBC Radio]], Tales of the Bizarre (December 7, 1995 to December 25, 1997) on [[org|org.deepv2.507b7f3aadcb7123|BBC Radio 4]], and Modern BBC Radio 4 revivals (May 22, 2007 to June 21, 2014) on [[org|org.deepv2.507b7f3aadcb7123|BBC Radio 4]].

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are Hamish Wilson (director on 8 recordings), Brian Sibley (radio adaptor on 6 recordings), Catherine Czerkawska (radio adaptor on 6 recordings), Adrian Bean (director on 2 recordings), Martin Jenkins (director on 2 recordings), Andrew Mark Sewell (director on 1 recording), and Bernadette Windsor (performer on 1 recording).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include Ray Bradbury work adapted for BBC radio, Tales of the Bizarre BBC Radio 4 anthology, supernatural, uncanny and macabre, science fiction and speculative futures, technology, automation and media anxiety, and Mars, spaceflight and cosmic isolation.

GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including Ray Bradbury’s Tales of the Bizarre, Bradbury and BBC radio across five decades, Early BBC Ray Bradbury radio adaptations, and BBC Bradbury productions in 1982.
plain_text:
Curated 21-item BBC Ray Bradbury radio-drama collection spanning 1962-2014. It combines standalone BBC adaptations with the 12-episode 1995-97 Tales of the Bizarre run and later Radio 4 Dangerous Visions productions. Frozen rows have no broadcast dates; historical production dates are represented additively in archive profiles and claims.

GRH documents the program through Early BBC Bradbury adaptations (September 12, 1962 to May 3, 1968) on BBC Radio, 1982-1991 BBC adaptations (1982-03 to August 28, 1991) on BBC Radio, Tales of the Bizarre (December 7, 1995 to December 25, 1997) on BBC Radio 4, and Modern BBC Radio 4 revivals (May 22, 2007 to June 21, 2014) on BBC Radio 4.

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are Hamish Wilson (director on 8 recordings), Brian Sibley (radio adaptor on 6 recordings), Catherine Czerkawska (radio adaptor on 6 recordings), Adrian Bean (director on 2 recordings), Martin Jenkins (director on 2 recordings), Andrew Mark Sewell (director on 1 recording), and Bernadette Windsor (performer on 1 recording).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include Ray Bradbury work adapted for BBC radio, Tales of the Bizarre BBC Radio 4 anthology, supernatural, uncanny and macabre, science fiction and speculative futures, technology, automation and media anxiety, and Mars, spaceflight and cosmic isolation.

GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including Ray Bradbury’s Tales of the Bizarre, Bradbury and BBC radio across five decades, Early BBC Ray Bradbury radio adaptations, and BBC Bradbury productions in 1982.
